Case 5:25-cv-04033-BLF          Document 58       Filed 06/10/25      Page 1 of 4




                                   1

                                   2

                                   3                                 UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

                                   4                             NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

                                   5                                        SAN JOSE DIVISION

                                   6

                                   7     GOOGLE LLC,                                      Case No. 5:25-cv-04033-BLF
                                   8                    Plaintiff,
                                                                                          ORDER DENYING GOOGLE LLC’S
                                   9             v.                                       MOTION TO ENLARGE DEADLINES
                                                                                          FOR DISCOVERY AND ADDITIONAL
                                  10     POINT FINANCIAL, INC.,                           PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION
                                                                                          BRIEFING, CONTINUE
                                  11                    Defendant.                        PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION
                                                                                          HEARING DATE, AND EXTEND
                                  12                                                      TEMPORARY RESTRAINING ORDER
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13                                                      [Re: Dkt. No. 45]
                                  14

                                  15          Before the Court is Plaintiff Google LLC’s (“Google”) Emergency Motion to Enlarge

                                  16   Deadlines for Discovery and Additional Preliminary Injunction Briefing, Continue Preliminary

                                  17   Injunction Hearing Date, and Extend Temporary Restraining Order. Dkt. No. 45 (“Mot.”).

                                  18   Defendant Point Financial, Inc. (“PFI”) filed a response to the motion. Dkt. No. 57 (“Resp.”).

                                  19          For the following reasons, the Court DENIES Google’s motion.

                                  20     I.   BACKGROUND
                                  21          Google initiated this action on May 8, 2025, simultaneously filing its Complaint, Dkt. No.

                                  22   1 (“Compl.”), and Motion for a Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction, Dkt.

                                  23   No. 3 (“TRO Mot.”). Pursuant to the Court’s Order Setting Briefing Schedule and Hearing on

                                  24   Motion for Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction, Dkt. No. 11, PFI filed a

                                  25   brief in opposition to Google’s Motion for a Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary

                                  26   Injunction, Dkt. No. 30, and Google filed a reply in support of its motion, Dkt. No. 32. The Court

                                  27   held a hearing on May 19, 2025, see Dkt. No. 35, at which it orally issued a temporary restraining

                                  28   order that was later memorialized in writing, see Dkt. No. 39 (“TRO Order”). The Court also set a
                                         Case 5:25-cv-04033-BLF           Document 58          Filed 06/10/25    Page 2 of 4




                                   1   preliminary injunction hearing for July 10, 2025, for which briefing would close on June 26, 2025.

                                   2   Id. at 13–14. Since the hearing on Google’s TRO, the Parties have been engaged in expedited

                                   3   discovery, including both written discovery and depositions. See Declaration of Morgan S. Birch

                                   4   in Support of Google LLC’s Emergency Motion to Enlarge Deadlines for Discovery and

                                   5   Additional Preliminary Injunction Briefing, Continue Preliminary Injunction Hearing Date, and

                                   6   Extend Temporary Restraining Order (“Birch Decl.”) ¶¶ 9–18, 22–25. Google now asserts that the

                                   7   “time allotted for expedited discovery is insufficient” and moves to extend the preliminary

                                   8   injunction hearing date and associated briefing and discovery deadlines. See Mot. at 1; Birch

                                   9   Decl. ¶¶ 4–5.

                                  10    II.   LEGAL STANDARD
                                  11          Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 6, “[w]hen an act may or must be done within a

                                  12   specified time, the court may, for good cause, extend the time” based on a motion made “before
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   the original time or its extension expires.” Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b)(1)(A). District courts often grant

                                  14   such requests in the absence of bad faith or prejudice to the adverse party, but the rule is

                                  15   discretionary; the Rule “provides that the court may grant the motion for good cause, not that it

                                  16   must do so.” Tindall v. First Solar Inc., 892 F.3d 1043, 1048 (9th Cir. 2018) (emphasis in

                                  17   original) (citing Ahanchian v. Xenon Pictures, Inc., 624 F.3d 1253, 1259 (9th Cir. 2010)). “‘Good

                                  18   cause’ is a non-rigorous standard that has been construed broadly.” Ahanchian, 624 F.3d at 1259.

                                  19   III.   DISCUSSION
                                  20          Google argues that there is good cause to enlarge the time for discovery and to extend the

                                  21   preliminary injunction hearing date and briefing deadlines, because “Google requires additional

                                  22   time to identify, collect, review, and produce documents responsive to PFI’s discovery requests.”

                                  23   Mot. at 4. In addition, Google says that it “requires additional time to review and analyze the

                                  24   contents of [a] hard drive recently produced by PFI,” and that both Parties “require additional time

                                  25   to take depositions relevant to the preliminary injunction briefing and hearing.” Id. Accordingly,

                                  26   Google requests a thirty-day extension of time to conduct discovery and to file supplemental briefs

                                  27   related to the preliminary injunction. Id. Google also asks the Court to reschedule the preliminary

                                  28   injunction hearing to a date after August 7, 2025. Id. At the same time, Google asks for the TRO
                                                                                          2
                                         Case 5:25-cv-04033-BLF           Document 58          Filed 06/10/25     Page 3 of 4




                                   1   to be extended until the new preliminary injunction hearing date, arguing that “[c]ourts routinely

                                   2   extend TROs in advance of preliminary injunction hearings to enable the parties to conduct

                                   3   relevant discovery and to submit full and complete briefing on the preliminary injunction papers.”

                                   4   Id. at 4–5 (citing Eurofins Elec. & Elec. Testing NA, LLC v. SGS N. Am. Inc., No. 5:24-cv-06340,

                                   5   2024 WL 4453315, at *3 (N.D. Cal. Oct. 8, 2024), and Salazar-Leyva v. Sessions, No. 17-cv-

                                   6   04213, 2017 WL 3232519, at *3 n.3 (N.D. Cal. July 28, 2017)). Google states that “[t]he same

                                   7   factual record that previously justified issuance of the TRO justifies extending it.” Id. at 5.

                                   8          PFI filed a response to Google’s administrative motion. Dkt. No. 57. Therein, PFI “agrees

                                   9   to moving the Order to Show Cause hearing as to the TRO enjoining PFI from taking further

                                  10   possession of certain products which Google alleges contain trade secrets and from disclosing,

                                  11   selling or licensing the products to third parties,” because that portion of the TRO is “fact-

                                  12   intensive and will require substantially more discovery.” Resp. at 4. However, “PFI opposes
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   moving the Order to Show Cause hearing as to the TRO enjoining PFI from contacting the

                                  14   Vendors and taking any action intended to or having the effect of interfering with Google’s

                                  15   licenses and access rights to certain IP” for three reasons: First, that portion of the TRO “enables

                                  16   Google to utilize CNEX intellectual property without compensation; second, “minimal discovery

                                  17   is needed to fully brief that issue;” and third, “Google should not be granted a delay that was

                                  18   caused by Google’s refusal to cooperate.” Id. PFI also purports to “cross move[] for the Court to

                                  19   (1) compel Google to comply with the Court’s previous order that it post security; (2) set specific

                                  20   expedited discovery deadlines; and (3) compel Google’s responses to discovery.” Id.

                                  21          As a preliminary matter, PFI’s opposition brief fails to comply with the Civil Local Rules,

                                  22   because it exceeds the allowed page limits. See Civ. L.R. 6-3(b). Accordingly, the Court will

                                  23   consider only the first five pages of argument and STRIKES pages 9 through 15 of the brief.

                                  24          Although it disregards the majority of PFI’s brief, the Court still concludes that Google has

                                  25   failed to show good cause for its requested extension. Google insisted at the TRO hearing that it

                                  26   sought a rapid resolution to this dispute, yet it appears that Google has engaged in various efforts

                                  27   to stonewall PFI during the Parties’ expedited discovery. See Resp. at 5; Declaration of Maria

                                  28   Crimi Speth in Support of Point Financial, Inc.’s Response to Google, LLC’s Emergency Motion
                                                                                          3
                                         Case 5:25-cv-04033-BLF           Document 58         Filed 06/10/25    Page 4 of 4




                                   1   and Emergency Cross Motion to Compel (“Speth Decl.”) ¶¶ 2–13. Google was aware, given the

                                   2   preliminary injunction hearing date that it accepted at the TRO hearing, that discovery would need

                                   3   to happen extremely quickly, yet it does not appear to have acted with appropriate haste in the

                                   4   days following that hearing. See, e.g., Speth Decl. ¶ 10 (noting that as of June 4, 2025, Google’s

                                   5   counsel had not assessed the relevant Google witnesses’ availability for depositions); id. ¶ 13

                                   6   (noting that Google did not produce written discovery responses until June 4, 2025, despite

                                   7   agreeing with PFI to a May 30, 2025 deadline, and that Google had not produced any documents

                                   8   as of June 9, 2025). The Court agrees with PFI that Google cannot profit from discovery delays of

                                   9   its own making. See Resp. at 6–7.

                                  10          Regarding the various requests posed in PFI’s opposition brief: First, the Court declines to

                                  11   bifurcate the order to show cause hearing. See Resp. at 4, 8. The Court issued one Temporary

                                  12   Restraining Order and will consider whether to issue a preliminary injunction as to some or all of
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   the conduct enjoined in that TRO at a single preliminary injunction hearing. Second, all discovery

                                  14   disputes in this matter are referred to the Magistrate Judge assigned to discovery, so PFI’s

                                  15   discovery-related requests should be posed to Judge Nathanael M. Cousins. Third, any request for

                                  16   affirmative relief must be asserted through an appropriate motion, so the Court will not consider or

                                  17   rule upon a purported “cross motion” included in a brief in opposition to another Party’s

                                  18   administrative motion. However, upon an appropriate motion, the Court will entertain a request to

                                  19   dissolve a TRO if bond is not posted immediately.

                                  20   IV.    ORDER
                                  21          For the foregoing reasons, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that Google LLC’s Emergency

                                  22   Motion to Enlarge Deadlines for Discovery and Additional Preliminary Injunction Briefing,

                                  23   Continue Preliminary Injunction Hearing Date, and Extend Temporary Restraining Order (Dkt.

                                  24   No. 45) is DENIED.

                                  25          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  26   Dated: June 10, 2025

                                  27                                                   ______________________________________
                                                                                       BETH LABSON FREEMAN
                                  28                                                   United States District Judge

                                  12    II.    LEGAL STANDARD
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13           The standard for issuing a temporary restraining order is identical to the standard for

                                  14   issuing a preliminary injunction. See Washington v. Trump, 847 F.3d 1151, 1159 n.3 (9th Cir.

                                  15   2017) (“[T]he legal standards applicable to TROs and preliminary injunctions are substantially

                                  16   identical.” (internal quotation marks and citation omitted)). An injunction is a matter of equitable

                                  18   the plaintiff is entitled to such relief.” Winter v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc., 555

                                  19   U.S. 7, 22 (2008). And “a TRO ‘should be restricted to . . . preserving the status quo and

                                  20   preventing irreparable harm just so long as is necessary to hold a [preliminary injunction] hearing

                                  21   and no longer.’” E. Bay Sanctuary Covenant v. Trump, 932 F.3d 742, 779 (9th Cir. 2018)

                                  22   (quoting Granny Goose Foods, Inc. v. Brotherhood of Teamsters & Auto Truck Drivers Local No.

                                  23   70, 415 U.S. 423, 439 (1974)).

                                  27   interest.” Winter, 555 U.S. at 20. “[I]f a plaintiff can only show that there are serious questions

                                  28   going to the merits—a lesser showing than likelihood of success on the merits—then a preliminary
                                                                                           4

                                   1   injunction may still issue if the balance of hardships tips sharply in the plaintiff’s favor, and the

                                  12   on the merits for all three claims.

                                  26                               ” to reassure the vendor of Google’s rights to the
